title: Standing-allowance elimination
models: Unvalidated arbitrary-call routers abusing standing ERC-20 allowances (two aggregator drains Jan 2026, ~$13.4M and ~$3.67M; a helper-contract drain 2025, ~$5M)
notes: Phase A: an unlimited standing allowance let the attacker's own later transaction move the victim's tokens.
Phase B: the victim approved exactly what was consumed and the POST_TX frame proved no allowance survived, so the attacker's identical transaction had nothing to take.
The attacker's transaction is never reverted by EIP-7906. What changed is that the standing allowance it depended on no longer exists.
Negative control: an over-approving bundle was invalidated, and no allowance was left behind (residual 0).

negative_control.description: over-approving leaves a residual allowance, so the guard invalidates the victim's own transaction rather than letting a drainable allowance persist
